summary: Kufra Airport (AKF) is a medium-sized regional airport serving the remote oasis city of Kufra in southeastern Libya, deep within the Libyan Desert near the borders with Egypt and Chad. As one of the few modern aviation gateways in this isolated desert region, it primarily supports domestic connectivity to Tripoli and Benghazi, as well as limited charter and humanitarian flights. The airport is vital for serving the local population of the Kufra oasis, one of the largest in the Sahara.
faqs:
Q: What airlines operate from Kufra Airport?
A: The airport is primarily served by Libyan carriers providing domestic flights, mainly to Tripoli (Mitiga) and Benghazi, with occasional charter operations.

Q: How far is Kufra Airport from the city center?
A: The airport is located a short drive from the town of Kufra, which is a relatively compact oasis settlement.

Q: Is Kufra Airport open to international flights?
A: The airport handles mostly domestic traffic, with occasional regional or humanitarian flights due to its proximity to remote desert areas and border regions.

Q: What facilities are available at the airport?
A: As a medium-sized regional facility, it offers basic passenger services, but amenities are limited compared to major international airports.
transport_tips: Taxis are typically available at the airport for the short journey into Kufra town, though pre-arranging transport is advisable given the limited options. Rental cars are generally not available at the airport, so travelers usually rely on hotel transfers or local drivers. Roads connecting the airport to the town are paved but remote, so plan travel during daylight hours.
local_tip: Bring plenty of water and sun protection even for short waits—Kufra sits in one of the hottest and driest parts of the Sahara, and shade is scarce around the airport grounds.
